_note_daily_overhead_day_model: days = setup + rate x SQ, least-squares fit over Tim's 30-home TIME LEARNING log (docs/ROOFR_OVERHEAD_TIERS.md). Tile R2 0.70 / Metal 0.66 fit well; demo+shingle are noisy (R2 ~0.37) — refit when Tim logs tear-off type. Low-slope systems are deliberately absent: no fitted data, so their labor days stay manual.

daily_overhead_day_model._note_geometry_model: days = intercept + coef*feature over RoofR cut measurements, fitted per series on Tim's 30-home log with NON-NEGATIVE coefficients (scripts/fit_days_from_roofr.py). Preferred over the squares-only fit above whenever a quote carries cut LFs, because Tim's method is time-driven and time tracks complexity, not area (Zoom 2026-07-17 [10:12]). Leave-one-out R2 in loo_r2. Negative coefficients are eliminated on purpose: 'more valleys means fewer days' is noise, and it under-prices the complex roofs that actually take longer.

pitch_day_adder._note: Steep-roof day adder. Tim books more time than the geometry model predicts on steep roofs: measured residual -0.29 days at <=4/12, +0.03 at 5/12, +0.64 at >=6/12 across his 29 homes. Applied to the INSTALL series only, once per job. A threshold rule rather than a fitted coefficient because only 7 of the 29 homes are >=6/12 and pitch as a regressor made every install series worse out-of-sample. NO homes in the sample are >=7/12, where Tim's own sheet says cost jumps ($305/sq tile adder) — revisit when he labels steeper roofs.

_note_overhead_basis: How a day of overhead is priced. 'branch' = ONE number per branch (monthly fixed overhead, calculated outside this system, divided by the working days in a month) x the days the job runs — Jon 2026-07-28, and Tim 2026-07-27 'my branch is like 28 grand... divide that by 20 work days'. 'series' = the legacy per-activity rates Tim emailed 2026-07-24 ($1,050 demo / $745 tile / $700 shingle / $850 metal). Defaults to 'series' because the two disagree by ~1.7x: against Tim's 21 actual sold prices the series rates land at +1.0% median, a flat $1,400/day at +13.3% with 19 of 21 below his own $2,500/week floor. Which is correct is a business decision (Jarvis #431) — the mechanism ships first, the switch flips after Tim answers.

_source_profit_floor: Tim, email 2026-07-10 'Re: Requested documents': "I generally like to make $2,500 min. per week the crew will be on-site.... Even though the total is 7 days of work, on a 40 SQ metal roof, I would charge closer to $5,000 at a min. for profit, because it's still taking up 2 weeks of work in window after inspections. A smaller roof that might be 8 squares and take 1.5 days, I would still want to make at least $2,500 on." 5-day week (Jon 2026-07-27; also what Tim's Miramar commercial calculator states twice). ceil(7/5)=2 weeks = $5,000, matching his worked example exactly; ceil(1.5/5)=1 week = $2,500, matching the small-roof half.
_scopes_doc: Which values a 'copy config to other branches' action may propagate. Jon, 2026-07-27: 'material cost should be shared by default, overhead and labor costs are branch specific.' shared = one company, one rule or one negotiated price. branch = what THIS branch's crews and office actually cost. mixed = the key fuses labour and material in one figure (Tim prices everything L+M+OH+P), so it cannot be classified until those are split; never copied. unclassified = the key's SHAPE is wrong (commission_pct is per salesperson, not per zone) and must be re-keyed before it can be scoped. An absent key defaults to 'branch' — fail closed, so a key nobody thought about is never propagated silently. Classification only: it moves no numbers, and scripts/seed_config_scopes.py asserts that.
